title: CraftableItem blob: what is proved, and what is sealed
context: the crafting line needed field semantics for the 124-byte CraftableItem blob. This records what the static analysis DID establish at instruction level, the method rules that invalidated three earlier attempts, and the one condition needed to finish.

layout.independent_confirmation: -[CraftableItemObject setCraftableItem:]'s own type encoding is v132@0:4{CraftableItem=ii[8i][8i]iiiSSi[8i]}8 - the same layout arrives from a method signature, not only from the savedict read length. Two independent sources now agree.

struct_is_passed_by_value.consequence: the 51 sites that copy 124 bytes are the by-value argument/return copies of this struct, not 'a bulk copy into an object'. Field reads therefore sit on caller stack buffers.

chain: 0xac79f4 ldr r3, [r2]  ; r3 = the ivar offset taken from a .got slot
0xac79f8 add r1, r1, r3; r1 = self + offset   (the ivar offset is 4)
read_back_from_the_save.verdict: instruction-level confirmation of the previously recorded line [[saveDict objectForKey:@"craftableItem"] getBytes:&self->craftableItem length:124]. An earlier claim of mine that the library has only ONE getBytes:length: reference (a 10-byte UINib path) was WRONG - a tool-coverage artefact.

chain: 0xac7c28 add r2, fp, #8     ; r2 = &(the by-value struct argument)
0xac7c4c ldr r1, [ip]       ; r1 = the ivar offset from a .got slot (=4)
0xac7c50 add r0, r0, r1     ; r0 = self+4 = &self->craftableItem

sites: 0xac7ccc - an initialiser (super dispatch then return self); role inferred from shape, not proved by name
the_ivar_has_three_reference_sites.consequence: no field read touches the cell, because consumers hold the struct by value or by pointer

selector_addressing_has_a_third_form.form: ldr ip,[pc,#k] ; add ip, ip, r1 ; ldr ip,[ip] ; blx - r1 is a PER-CLASS slot index
selector_addressing_has_a_third_form.consequence: find_selector_senders.py models only the pool+PIC form, so for getBytes:length: it reports slots=1 / sends=0 while real call sites exist (e.g. the Action site at 0x735be8, movw r3, #0xc). Empty results cover only the scanned channel.
selector_addressing_has_a_third_form.reliable_search: search the length immediate instead: movw r3,#0x7c (124) occurs exactly 5 times (CraftableItemObject -[initWithSaveDict:] 0xac7984, -[setCraftableItem:] 0xac7c2c, Workbench -[initWithWorld:...] 0xae594c, Workbench -[blockheadWouldLikeToTakeOwnership:...] 0xae7864, CraftUI -[updateTeleportCraftableItem] 0xb6b1a0); #0xc (12) occurs 19 times.

method_rules_earned_here: A small struct's field offsets collide numerically with stack-frame offsets, so matching an offset alone is invalid by construction - it produced a table of ~1600 'field accesses' that were all [sp, ...] frames.
Field access must first PROVE the base: track the register that receives self+cell for the ivar, or the destination of the by-value copy.
A fast alarm that a rule has not locked onto an object: the hits cover essentially every method in the library.
Empty results cover only the channel that was scanned (the getBytes:length: lesson).
dst/src forms read by 'last matching instruction before the call' are unreliable - here they produced a copy whose source and destination were the same stack slot.

sealed.what_is_not_done: field semantics for the 11 field offsets
sealed.condition_needed: a base-provenance tracker: instruction-level register/dataflow from the by-value buffer (the 124-byte copy destination) to each access, so that [sp, #k+field] can be distinguished from a genuine stack frame at the same offset. Offset heuristics cannot do it; three attempts failed and each was invalid by construction, not merely incomplete.
sealed.what_would_make_it_easy: a live CraftableItemObject instance to read (the current world has no workbench, so none exists), or a save containing a craftableItem blob paired with a known crafting state.
